chunk_a.text_snippet:
Title: RAF jets flying defensive missions after US-Israeli attack on Iran, Starmer says
Date: 2026-02-28

Content: Keir Starmer has said RAF fighter jets are flying “in the sky today” to defend allies in the Middle East against Iranian retaliation after the US and Israel launched a bombing campaign aimed at regime change in Tehran. The UK did not participate in the first waves of strikes against Iran on Saturday morning and has no immediate intention of doing so, but fighter jets were running defensive operations from Qatar and Cyprus to shoot down any incoming drones and missiles. Iran launched an immediate counterattack, including strikes on Israel and Jordan as well as on US bases in Bahrain, Qatar, United Arab Emirates and Kuwait. British forces are located at the bases in small numbers. Details of the operations were scant, and the Ministry of Defence would not specify which countries and bases were being defended, though the UK recently boosted deployments in case there was an escalation of hostilities.

chunk_b.text_snippet:
Title: Starmer says UK will not join ‘regime change from the skies’ on Iran
Date: 2026-03-02

Content: “The basis for our decision is the collective self-defence of longstanding friends and allies and protecting British lives. It is in accordance with international law.” He said the RAF had intercepted an Iranian drone strike heading for a coalition base in Iraq where UK forces were stationed. Two drones were also fired at the British base in Cyprus, RAF Akrotiri. Starmer said they were launched before Sunday’s night’s statement on the US use of UK bases. The defence secretary, John Healey, said the damage was minimal but that the UK was moving families who lived at RAF Akrotiri to alternative temporary accommodation in Cyprus. The base is not being used to launch US strikes. A Cypriot news agency reported the damage to the airbase was caused by small low-flying drones launched by Hezbollah, an Iranian proxy group from Lebanon – but the UK Ministry of Defence did not formally confirm that.

initial_question.rag_input: How did the RAF's defensive mission in the Middle East, launched on February 28, 2026, respond to the threat posed by Iranian retaliatory strikes against British assets?
initial_question.question: How did the RAF's defensive mission in the Middle East, launched on February 28, 2026, respond to the threat posed by Iranian retaliatory strikes against British assets?
initial_question.answer: Following the February 28, 2026, Iranian retaliatory strikes, the RAF began flying defensive missions from Qatar and Cyprus to intercept incoming drones and missiles; this defensive posture was specifically challenged when two drones were fired at RAF Akrotiri, which subsequently led the UK Ministry of Defence to relocate families living at the base to alternative temporary accommodation in Cyprus.
initial_question.bridging_topic: RAF defensive operations and the resulting safety measures for personnel after Iranian retaliation
